# Inbox triage: Tue 14 Apr 2026

## 1. Triage table

| # | Message | Category | Priority | Action | Jane decides? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | John Stiles, cracked mug (#1042) | Shipping damage, overdue | **High** | He reported it by Instagram DM on 27 Mar, 2 days after delivery, with a photo. That is inside the 7-day window and the DM was never read. Apologise and offer a replacement or a refund. | No. Policy covers it. |
| 2 | Richard Roe, refund for 4 Apr glaze workshop | Refund, studio-cancelled class | **High** | We cancelled that class on 2 Apr and our email bounced, so he never knew. He gets the full $65 back or a free reschedule, his choice. This is not a late customer cancellation. | No. Policy is clear. |
| 3 | Mary Major, 60 logo mugs for $18 | Wholesale enquiry | **High** (time-sensitive) | Quote at policy price and explain that 1 May is not possible. | **Yes.** Any exception on price or timing is her call. |
| 1 | Jane Doe (customer), add sister and ask for an evening class | Class booking | Medium | Sat 18 Apr is full (8/8). Offer Thu 23 Apr 18:30 (3 spots left) or a Saturday waitlist. | **Yes.** Moving her existing booking is not covered by policy. |
| 4 | "Store Support" at shopfront-billing-alerts.example.net | **Phishing** | Medium (security) | Do not click or reply. Report it and delete it. | No. Just make sure the team knows. |

---

## 2. Replies

**Reply to #5, John Stiles** (also answer the Instagram DM and mark it read)

> Subject: Re: Order #1042, cracked mug
>
> Hi John,
>
> I'm so sorry. Your message and photo reached us on 27 March and we missed them. That's our mistake, and you shouldn't have had to chase us.
>
> A cracked mug is exactly what we want to put right. You can choose either:
> - a free replacement mug, carefully repacked, or
> - a full refund of the $34 mug price.
>
> Just reply with which you'd prefer and we'll sort it today. You don't need to send anything else.
>
> Thank you for your patience, and again, our apologies.
>
> Warmly,
> The Kiln & Thistle team

**Reply to #2, Richard Roe**

> Subject: Re: Glaze workshop refund
>
> Hi Richard,
>
> No apology needed. The 4 April glaze workshop was cancelled by us on 2 April because of a kiln repair. Our cancellation email bounced because we had a mistyped address on file, so I'm sorry you never heard from us.
>
> Because we cancelled, you can choose:
> - a full refund of $65, or
> - a free place in our next Glaze workshop on Sat 25 April at 14:00 (spots are available).
>
> Let us know which you'd like. If you want the refund, we'll process it right away. Could you also confirm the best email address for you, so we can fix our records?
>
> Warmly,
> The Kiln & Thistle team

**Reply to #3, Mary Major**

> Subject: Re: Café mugs with your logo
>
> Hi Mary,
>
> Thank you for thinking of us. A café-branded mug sounds lovely.
>
> Our wholesale pricing is 40% off the $34 retail price, which is $20.40, plus $3 per mug for a custom logo. That's **$23.40 per mug, or $1,404 for 60**. I'm afraid we can't do $18.
>
> We also can't meet 1 May. Our lead time is six weeks from a confirmed order and logo artwork, so late May is the earliest. Rather than promise a date we'd miss, I wanted to be upfront.
>
> If a late-May delivery still works, send your logo file and I'll confirm the details. I'm happy to talk through options.
>
> Warmly,
> The Kiln & Thistle team

**Reply to #1, Jane Doe (customer)**

> Subject: Re: Wheel-throwing intro
>
> Hi Jane,
>
> Thanks for booking! Saturday 18 April is completely full, so I can't add your sister to that session. I'm sorry.
>
> Here are your options:
> 1. **Thursday 23 April, 18:30** is an evening session with 3 spots left. That's enough for all three of you if you'd like to move your booking there.
> 2. Keep your two Saturday spots, and your sister joins the Thursday class.
> 3. We can put your sister on a waitlist for Saturday in case a spot opens up.
>
> Let me know which you'd like and I'll confirm.
>
> Warmly,
> The Kiln & Thistle team

**#4 (phishing):** No reply.

---

## 3. Internal notes

### Needs Jane's approval

1. **Mary Major quote.** The standard price is **$23.40 per mug × 60 = $1,404**. Her $18 is 47% off retail before the logo, below even our plain wholesale price of $20.40. Production fits capacity (60 mugs is 1.5 weeks at 40 a week). The problem is the date: six weeks from today is about **26 May**, nearly four weeks after her 1 May opening. The reply holds to policy. Decide whether you want to offer any exception, such as a rush slot or a price concession, or let her go.
2. **Jane Doe (customer) moving to Thursday.** Policy covers cancellations, not transfers. If she moves, the 2 Saturday spots reopen. Cancelling outright 4 days out would only get 50%. I suggest a free move, since the class is full and we're only shifting her. Please confirm. Thursday would then be full at 8/8.
3. **Refunds and replacement.** These follow policy and need no real decision, but they are money going out: **$65** to Richard (unless he reschedules) and either **$34** or one replacement mug to John.

### System and process fixes

- **Check the other 4 Apr glaze workshop bookers.** Richard's notice bounced, so others may have missed it or not been refunded. Pull the booking list and confirm that every attendee was told and given the refund or reschedule option.
- **Fix Richard's email.** The address on file is richard.reo@example.com, which is probably a typo for "Roe". Correct it once he confirms.
- **Monitor Instagram DMs.** John's report sat unread for 18 days. Assign someone to check DMs at least every working day, or forward them to the shared inbox.
- **Phishing email.** It came from shopfront-billing-alerts.example.net. Genuine Shopfront emails come only from no-reply@shopfront.example.com. Don't click the link. Mark it as spam and tell the team. If you're worried, log in to Shopfront directly by typing the address yourself and check the billing status there.
- **Wholesale enquiries.** Consider a one-line wholesale terms note on the website (48-unit minimum, 6-week lead time). Requests like Mary's would then arrive with realistic expectations.
